answer: Sequential work receipts: each new identity must complete a verifiable task whose output depends on a prior agent's private state, and the receiving agent only accepts work after posting a small refundable deposit at a public wharf ledger. A clone must harbor a fresh state history, so it cannot reuse originals and must redo every prior task, paying compute and deposit lockup each time. Validators sample the chain and slash the deposit of any identity whose receipts fail replay against the recorded opal checkpoint.
